Subordinate

suh-BOR-din-it — as a noun, subordinate rhymes with 'coordinate'; 'sub-' means under, so a subordinate stands under someone else in rank. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Subordinate is a person who is under the authority of another; one who ranks below someone else.

As the newest subordinate on the crew, he double-checked every decision with the ship's captain.

Worked Example

In a large hospital, a new intern reports every patient update to the senior resident, who in turn reports to the attending physician, who reports to the department head.

Each person in that chain answers to the person directly above them -- that's exactly the relationship a subordinate has to their superior. Unlike 'colleague,' which implies equal standing, subordinate specifically means ranked below.

How Subordinate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

underling

underling: a person of low rank under another's authority

junior

junior: lower in rank or position

assistant

assistant: a person who helps and reports to someone of higher rank

Antonyms

superior

superior: a person of higher rank or authority

supervisor

supervisor: a person who oversees and directs others

How Strong Is It? — junior → subordinate → underling

junior vs. subordinate

junior vs. subordinate: Junior is milder than subordinate -- junior simply describes someone newer or lower-ranked, while subordinate specifically emphasizes that person's authority sits beneath someone else's.

underling vs. subordinate

underling vs. subordinate: Underling can feel harsher than subordinate: underling often carries a slightly negative, dismissive tone, while subordinate is a neutral, formal term for rank.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — sub-

prefix — sub-: under, below (Latin)

root — -ordin-

root — -ordin-: order, rank (Latin (ordo))

suffix — -ate

suffix — -ate: having the quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin ordo meant 'order, rank, row.' A subordinate is, at its root, someone placed in the rank directly under another -- literally 'under the order.'
